title: Which bot guards apply to a deliberate buy, and how does the operator confirm before it signs?

options.name: Keep current behaviour: affordability check only, 5-second Ctrl+C window
options.risk: Any typed amount the wallet can afford is bought (no risk gate, circuit breaker or pause); a typo or a wrong token goes out unless Ctrl+C lands within 5 seconds, and Ctrl+C through npx on Windows may not stop the script (AUD-SCRIPTS-004, S2).

options.name: Typed confirmation, guards unchanged
options.behavior_impact: after the banner the operator must type the amount and the last characters of the token address (or "yes") before anything is signed; no timed window
options.risk: Still bypasses the risk gate, circuit breaker and pause; a wrong but confirmed amount still goes out.

options.name: Typed confirmation plus the bot buy guards, with an explicit typed override
options.behavior_impact: the deliberate buy also passes the risk gate, the circuit breaker and the pause check; the operator can override a risk-gate refusal only by typing an override phrase that is logged and alerted
options.risk: A deliberate buy the operator really wants can be refused until they override; the override path needs its own test.

recommendation: guards-and-confirmation: a manual buy should not be the one buy that skips every limit, and a typed confirmation does not depend on how the terminal handles Ctrl+C. Decide with SCRIPTS-01 (pause check while holding the lock) and BUY-01.
default: Keep current behaviour until the owning phase rules (milestone contract); nothing changes in Phase 22. The bot is off for all of v7.0; deliberate buys are only run by the operator by hand.
behavior_impact: Decides which limits a manual buy respects and what the operator must do before it is signed.
needed_by: Phase 24 capital discussion (with BUY-01), or Phase 29 HYG-03 at the latest
